other_failure_modes.name: Independent test set parametric transformation
other_failure_modes.description: Applying a parameterized data transformation (like Yeo-Johnson) independently on the test set without saving and reusing the parameters learned from the training set. This maps the same raw feature values to different transformed values in train vs test, corrupting the feature space for inference.

other_failure_modes.name: Validation leakage during imputation
other_failure_modes.description: Computing imputation statistics (e.g., medians) on the entire training set before the cross-validation loop. This leaks validation fold statistics into the training folds, making the out-of-fold validation scores overly optimistic.

summary: The agent demonstrates strong practices overall, including excellent clinical feature engineering, a rigorous cross-validation setup, and proper logit-space ensembling. However, a critical flaw exists in the feature engineering pipeline where the Yeo-Johnson transformation is applied independently to the test set, meaning its transformation parameters are fit on test data rather than inherited from training data. Additionally, there is minor data leakage due to calculating imputation medians on the full training set prior to cross-validation.
